statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-22185 is a one-byte heap buffer underflow in the readline() function of mdb_load, the database load tool of LMDB (the Lightning Memory-Mapped Database bundled with OpenLDAP), in LMDB 0.9.14 before 0.9.34: malformed input with an embedded NUL byte can make mdb_load read before its buffer and crash. It is fixed by https://github.com/openldap/openldap/commit/8e1fda85532a3c74276df38a42d234dcdfa1e40d (https://bugs.openldap.org/show_bug.cgi?id=10421), which changes only libraries/liblmdb/mdb_load.c. The Debian tracker notes that the openldap source bundles LMDB but does not build mdb_load: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-22185. Unpacked every package of both builds published for this source in the DHI Debian repository for trixie (Debian version 2.6.10+dfsg-1), on amd64 and arm64: ldap-utils, libldap2, libldap-dev, libldap-common, libldap2-dev and the ldap-utils and libldap2 debug-symbol packages. DHI builds Debian's openldap source with Debian's pkg.openldap.noslapd build profile, which adds --disable-slapd to the configuration (https://sources.debian.org/src/openldap/2.6.10+dfsg-1/debian/rules/). The packages hold the ldap* command-line clients, the libldap and liblber shared libraries, their static archives libldap.a and liblber.a (client library objects only), headers, pkg-config files, the ldap.conf client configuration file, documentation, and debug symbols. No package contains mdb_load or any other LMDB program, library or object: no file name contains mdb or lmdb, and neither static archive has an LMDB member. slapd, whose mdb backend is the part of OpenLDAP that uses LMDB, is not built.
